newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Crippled beggar wins freedom in Hong Kong appeal.
newsitem.headline: Crippled beggar wins freedom in Hong Kong appeal.

text.p: A beggar crippled by polio who crawled his way into the headlines was freed on Tuesday when a Hong Kong court ruled in favour of his appeal against a six-month prison term, government radio reported.
Cheung Sun-wah was ordered released after winning his appeal against his conviction for arson, assaulting a police officer and being in the territory illegally, the report said.

Cheung, who had snuck into Hong Kong from China, was arrested in March while begging in the territory. He admitted striking a police officer with his crutches and burning three HK$100 (US$13) bills in his jail cell.
He became a cause celebre when he had to crawl on his belly into a magistrate's court in April because his crutches had been confiscated as evidence.
But while Cheung won his freedom, the High Court also ordered that he be deported back to China.
